# Philip Rubin — Summary
Philip Rubin is a distinguished scientist and administrator whose research integrates computational, engineering, linguistic, physiological, and psychological approaches, focusing on embodied cognition and the biological bases of speech and language. He is especially recognized for pioneering work in articulatory synthesis, speech perception, sinewave synthesis, perceptual organization, and the modeling of complex temporal speech events. At Haskins Laboratories, Rubin developed influential computational models including ASY (articulatory synthesis), CASY (configurable articulatory synthesizer), SWS (sinewave synthesis), and the TADA system for modeling speech coordination. His theoretical contributions shaped perspectives on speech as a dynamical system, emphasizing spatiotemporal coordination, perceptual organization, and the embodied nature of speech gestures; these advances have impacted both scientific research and technology.
Beyond his scientific contributions, Rubin played prominent roles in science policy and advocacy, including as Director of Behavioral and Cognitive Sciences at the National Science Foundation, Assistant Director at the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, and Chair of the National Academies Board on Behavioral, Cognitive, and Sensory Sciences. He was instrumental in launching initiatives such as the BRAIN Initiative and neuroscience-focused interagency collaborations. Rubin has been active in ethical oversight of research and technologies, notably in human subjects protection and the evaluation of emerging behavioral sciences. He has received numerous honors, including fellowships in major scientific associations, and has held leadership positions in several organizations including FABBS and Haskins Laboratories. Rubin's personal interests include photography, music, and contributions to popular culture through collaborations and technical advisement.
